glossary.Inflammatory: Driven by the immune response, causing redness, heat and swelling.
glossary.Skin barrier: The outer skin layer that keeps water in and irritants and microbes out.
glossary.Hypersensitivity: An exaggerated immune reaction to something usually harmless.
glossary.Asthma: Chronic inflammation and narrowing of the airways causing wheeze.
glossary.Allergic rhinitis: Inflamed nose lining from allergy: sneezing, runny or blocked nose.
glossary.Loss-of-function mutation: A gene change that stops the protein working properly.
glossary.Flare-ups: Periods when symptoms suddenly get worse.
glossary.Psoriasis: An immune skin disease with well-demarcated, scaly plaques, often on extensor surfaces.
glossary.Dust mites: Tiny bugs in house dust whose droppings are a common allergen.
glossary.Food allergies: Immune reactions to foods such as milk, egg or peanut.
glossary.Erosions: Shallow breaks in the skin surface.
glossary.Malaise: A general feeling of being unwell.
glossary.Coxsackievirus: An enterovirus that causes hand, foot and mouth disease.
glossary.Secondary bacterial infection: Bacteria infecting skin already damaged by eczema.
glossary.Allergy testing: Tests to find what a person is allergic to.
glossary.Dermatology: The medical specialty of skin disease.
glossary.Epaderm: A brand of greasy emollient ointment.
glossary.Hydromol: A brand of emollient ointment or cream.
glossary.Potency: How strong a topical steroid is: mild, moderate, potent or very potent.
glossary.Flexures: Skin creases such as the inside of the elbow and back of the knee.
glossary.Systemic therapy: Tablets or injections acting on the whole body, used for severe eczema.
glossary.S. aureus: Staphylococcus aureus, the bacterium that most often infects eczema.
glossary.Flucloxacillin: A penicillin antibiotic used for staphylococcal skin infection.
glossary.Allergens: Substances that trigger an allergic reaction.
glossary.Irritants: Substances that damage skin directly, such as soaps and detergents.
glossary.B cells: White blood cells that make antibodies such as IgE.
glossary.Predisposition: A tendency to develop a condition.
glossary.Epidermal: Relating to the epidermis, the outer layer of skin.
glossary.Melanocyte: A skin cell that makes the pigment melanin.
